# Agent-Ready Score

> Free OpenAPI lint plus a deterministic documentation checklist. Static analysis of the spec — not a runtime test of agents.

- Live tool: https://validator.appear.sh
- Source: https://github.com/appear-sh/api-validator
- Originally from Appear (wound down). Founders now build https://www.ctxpipe.ai

## What it does

Upload or paste an OpenAPI 3.0.x, 3.1, or 3.2 spec (YAML or JSON). The tool runs three technical validators (Spectral, Swagger Parser, OAS Zod Validator) and a deterministic checklist score. No account. No model in the scoring loop. Same spec, same score.

OpenAPI 3.2 is checked by OAS Zod Validator only. Spectral and Swagger Parser are skipped until those engines support 3.2.

## Agent-Ready Score

A rule-based 0–100 checklist of what is written in the specification: parseability, descriptions, operationIds, examples, documented auth, and documented errors. Grade A/B (80+) means strong coverage of this checklist, not that the API is “agent ready”.

| Dimension | Weight | What it checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Foundational Compliance | 25% | Spec parses; broken $refs and invalid schemas stop document consumers |
| Semantic Richness | 20% | Descriptions present in the spec |
| Agent Usability | 20% | operationIds, idempotency and pagination as documented |
| AI Discoverability | 15% | Examples and tags |
| Security | 10% | Documented auth schemes (not a live auth test) |
| Error Recoverability | 10% | Documented error schemas (not live Retry-After) |

This is not an AI judge and not a certification.

## What it is not

ctxpipe.ai is a separate product: a self-learning context layer for AI engineering agents. This validator does not auto-fix specs and is not a ctxpipe feature.
